record.paper_title: Unfolding the Labyrinth: Open Problems in Physics, Mathematics, Astrophysics and Other Areas of Science
record.original_question: What are the correct relativistic answers to the problems listed here, including the geometry of a relativistically rotating plane, whether rotating free-fall systems obey the equivalence principle in the expected way, how dropped objects and projectiles behave in the airplane-and-elevator thought experiment, and whether temperature can affect spacetime curvature or the metric itself?

evidence.quote: Questions: i. What is the geometric shape of a relativistic rotating plane (Unruh experiment)? Is it Minkowskian, Euclidean, or Riemannian?
v. What is the effect of space temperature on the spacetime curvature? Or does temperature affect the metric of spacetime?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Within the framework of general relativity and special relativity, provide rigorous answers to the following thought-experiment questions:

(i) Consider a rigid plane disk rotating with constant angular velocity about its center, observed from an inertial frame in Minkowski spacetime. Taking into account length contraction of circumferential elements but not of radial elements (the Ehrenfest setup), determine the intrinsic geometry experienced by co-rotating observers on the disk: is the induced spatial metric flat (Euclidean), Minkowskian, or a non-flat Riemannian metric of nonzero Gaussian curvature? Give an explicit form of the spatial metric and its curvature.

(ii) Consider a system in free fall that is simultaneously rotating (for example, a freely falling laboratory spinning about an axis through its center of mass). Does Einstein's equivalence principle apply in the usual local sense to such a rotating freely falling frame? Identify precisely which tidal/Coriolis/centrifugal effects can or cannot be eliminated by passing to a freely falling rotating frame, and state in what sense (if any) the equivalence principle holds.

(iii) (Airplane-and-elevator thought experiment.) An airplane moves with constant horizontal velocity relative to the ground in a uniform gravitational field. Inside the airplane an "elevator" cabin is in free fall. Determine the trajectories, as seen by (a) a ground-based observer, (b) an observer at rest in the airplane, and (c) an observer inside the freely falling cabin, of: an object released from rest within the cabin, and a projectile launched horizontally within the cabin. Show consistency of the three descriptions via the appropriate coordinate transformations.

(iv) In the Einstein field equations G_{μν} = 8πG T_{μν}, the stress–energy tensor T_{μν} of a relativistic fluid or radiation field depends on its temperature (e.g., through energy density and pressure of a thermal distribution). Determine quantitatively whether and how the temperature of matter/radiation filling a region of space affects the spacetime curvature and the metric, and identify whether "temperature" enters the metric in any way beyond its contribution to T_{μν}.
artifact.status_search_result: These are classical conceptual/pedagogical questions in relativity (Ehrenfest paradox, equivalence principle in rotating frames, free-fall thought experiments, thermal contributions to T_{μν}). The Ehrenfest rotating-disk problem is widely discussed and the standard answer (a non-Euclidean spatial metric in the co-rotating frame) is well established, though debate over interpretation persists. The other items are largely textbook exercises rather than open research problems. No definitive single "solution" reference resolves all four parts as posed; status overall is best described as unknown/not a sharply formulated open problem.
